facts.text: Malta, Idaho was named after the Mediterranean island because early settlers felt it was an island amid the wide expanse of the Raft River Valley.
In the early 1880s, settlers had no central mail spot; the Condit family secured a permit, and a post office opened in 1883, naming the town.
It also has histories and information from Raft River High School, including yearbooks.
A website, created as an Eagle Scout project, includes a history on the majority of the people buried at the Valley Vu Cemetery in Malta.
The Malta, Idaho History Archive describes the town as an island of memory nestled within the Raft River Valley.
Church history in Malta traces community gathering places and faith traditions that have shaped local life for generations.
